title: A ticket's status: show it moving along
question: You said the status row looks like tabs, not a progression. Three ways to show a ticket moving New → In progress → Fixed, to check → Resolved, in the docked ticket and its page. Each says the files go 7 days after closing. Lock one, steer it, or ask for another hand.

options.label: Stage track with a next step
options.thesis: The four stages as a track of dots joined by a line: passed ones filled in deep aqua, the current one ringed. Under it, one primary button for the next step (Mark fixed, to check →) and Mark not doing. Click any stage to jump there.
options.viewport: Docked ticket: title and #42, the track with New done and In progress current, Mark fixed, to check → beside Mark not doing, the 7-day line.
options.risk: Takes two rows instead of one; the stage labels are small at the dock's narrowest (360px).

options.label: One button: the next step
options.thesis: Where it is now as a status pill with who moved it and when, then one primary button for the obvious next step and a Move to… menu for anything else.
options.viewport: Docked ticket: the In progress pill with 'since 9:52am, by Claude', Mark fixed, to check, Move to…, Not doing, the 7-day line.
options.risk: You don't see all the stages at a glance; going back a step is in a menu.

options.label: Pipeline of arrows
options.thesis: Arrow-shaped stages left to right: passed ones ticked and tinted, the current one filled in deep aqua. Click a stage to move it there; Mark not doing under it.
options.viewport: Docked ticket: the arrows with New ticked and In progress filled, Mark not doing, the 7-day line.
options.risk: Still one row of four clickable parts; labels wrap to two lines in the narrow dock.
